title: Parallelizable Exact Synthesis of Quantum Circuits via Semi-Tensor Product
authors: Chenjian Li, Dingchao Gao, Xiangzhen Zhou, Ji Guan, Pengcheng Zhu, Zhufei Chu
abstract: Exact synthesis is a useful tool in quantum compilation by providing optimal alternative implementations of small circuit shards and is widely used as a circuit re-synthesis optimization kernel. However, existing exact synthesis methods suffer from encoding overhead, poor parallel scalability, and memory bottlenecks. This paper introduces a parallel exact synthesis framework for CNOT and phase polynomial circuits, which is based on the semi-tensor product (STP) theory of matrices. By enumerating undirected partial-gate topologies and solving the missing gate directions separately, we are able to parallelize both stages and achieve a parallel speedup of up to $12.8\times$ with 32 workers on this NP-hard problem. More specifically, for each topology, the circuit semantics are converted into canonical STP formulas, and feasibility is decided by a right-to-left factorization procedure that removes infeasible direction assignments. On randomly generated synthesis targets, STP is typically $100\times-1000\times$ faster than the SAT-based baseline on small instances, and remains competitive for more difficult instances. When integrated in a real-world circuit optimization workflow, our algorithm outperforms the SAT-based approach on 89% of cases in QASMBench, and achieves a median speedup of $1.91\times$.
summary: This work presents a novel, parallel exact synthesis framework for optimizing quantum circuits using the Semi-Tensor Product (STP) theory. By efficiently solving circuit constraints derived from CNOT and phase polynomial gates, it significantly outperforms existing SAT-based methods on benchmark tests. This advancement provides a powerful kernel for improving overall quantum compilation workflows.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of exact synthesis for quantum circuits, which is crucial for optimizing small circuit shards in quantum compilation.
main_result: The proposed Semi-Tensor Product (STP) framework achieves significant parallel speedups (up to 12.8x on random circuits) compared to SAT-based methods when synthesizing CNOT and phase polynomial circuits.
method: It introduces a parallel exact synthesis framework based on STP theory, decomposing the problem into topology enumeration and solving missing gate directions via canonical STP factorization procedures.
model_or_system: The system is quantum computation using qubits, where circuit semantics are modeled by linear parity matrices (for CNOT) or phase polynomials ($Rz$ gates).
key_observables: Computational speedup factor, synthesis feasibility, and the number of required gates/circuit size.
important_parameters: The complexity is NP-hard; performance is measured against SAT-based baselines on benchmarks like QASMBench.
main_assumptions: Existing methods suffer from encoding overhead (SAT) or memory bottlenecks; the STP approach assumes that circuit constraints can be mapped to solvable canonical STP formulas.
figures_summary: Figures compare parallel speedups of STP against SAT/Gimsatul on random circuits and show end-to-end runtime comparisons across different gate count regimes of QASMBench.
paper_structure: The paper details the need for exact synthesis, introduces the STP theory as a solution, presents the framework involving topology enumeration and factorization, and validates its performance against state-of-the-art methods on established benchmarks.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum computation optimization rather than AMO dynamics, the underlying mathematical tools (tensor products, algebraic structure analysis) are highly relevant to characterizing entanglement structures or simulating complex multi-body interactions in open quantum systems.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Overall structure of our STP-based synthesis algorithm for a fixed gate count (#g). Given a synthesis target, candidate topologies are enumerated, while infeasible ones are eliminated through pruning. Each surviving topology is then passed to an STP-based circuit solver, which either proves it unsatisfiable or returns a complete circuit implementation. Both topology enumeration and circuit solving can be processed in parallel, since different topologies can be handled independently.
Fig. 2. Runtime of STP against Qiskit-SAT on random CNOT circuits. For each data point, 10 random circuits are generated and tested. The timeout value is set to 600 seconds.
Fig. 3. Parallel speedup of STP against Qiskit-SAT with the Gimsatul backend [29] with 32 workers on random CNOT circuits. For each data point, 10 random circuits are generated and tested.

Fig. 4. Optimization runtime of Gimsatul, STP and STP+Gimsatul portfolio on QASMBench. Left: QASMBench cases with gate count smaller than 100; Middle: Cases with gate count greater than 100 but smaller than 1000; Right: Cases with gate count greater than 1,000 but smaller than 10,000.
